mission: The Midas Project is a watchdog that investigates whether AI companies keep their safety promises, applying corporate-accountability tactics to the AI industry. It tracks quiet changes to company safety policies (Watchtower), publishes investigations and analysis of AI lobbying (Model Republic), and pushes for transparency.

key_work.title: The OpenAI Files
key_work.plain_summary: With the Tech Oversight Project, a 50+ page collection of documented concerns about OpenAI's governance, leadership integrity and culture as it moved from nonprofit to for-profit.

key_work.title: Watchtower
key_work.plain_summary: A running tracker of changes to, and violations of, AI companies' published safety policies and model cards.

key_work.title: Seoul Tracker
key_work.plain_summary: Grades whether AI companies are keeping the voluntary safety commitments they made at the 2024 Seoul AI Summit.

key_work.title: Open letter calling for OpenAI transparency
key_work.plain_summary: An open letter, signed by 100+ experts, ex-OpenAI staff and groups, asking OpenAI to answer questions about its restructuring.

key_work.title: IRS complaint about OpenAI
key_work.plain_summary: A complaint alleging possible tax-law violations at OpenAI, including board conflicts of interest.

status_note: watchdog nonprofit; received subpoenas from OpenAI in Aug 2025 during the Musk v. OpenAI litigation

warnings.text: AI companies quietly change or weaken their own safety policies without public notice.
Companies may break new AI transparency laws (Midas alleged OpenAI violated California's SB 53 in 2026).
OpenAI's shift away from nonprofit control may strip the public of protections it was promised.
Legal pressure such as subpoenas can be used to slow down small nonprofit critics.

recommendations.text: Make AI companies publicly accountable for keeping their safety commitments.
Require transparency about which models are covered by safety laws and publish safety reports on time.
Preserve meaningful nonprofit control over OpenAI.
